current.text: He is out with a health issue. He missed media day and the preseason. Reports differ on the cause: one note names a hamstring injury, while others say it is unclear what is wrong.
The Warriors give no updates on his status, and Steve Kerr keeps saying he does not know. When he will return is unknown.
He re-signed with Golden State for 3 years and 40 million USD with a player option, with 20 million guaranteed. The plan is for him to start at center when healthy.
While he is out, the Warriors start Draymond Green at center, with Podziemski and Lendeborg also in the lineup.

Experts now say not to draft him. They do not know if he will play again and expect probably nothing from him. One calls him his biggest Warriors fade and would take him around pick 100 only in stash formats.
In mid-October expert mock drafts he went around picks 137 to 164.

When he plays, experts see his per game value far above his draft spot, somewhere between top 30 and top 70. One sees roughly 40th-ranked per game value, and another sees top 70 value over about 40 games.
Golden State has 15 back-to-backs, tied for second most. One expert counts three back-to-backs in the recommended playoff window, so he would likely get 8 games there instead of 11.
The Warriors may treat this as a throwaway or gap year. They worry about lottery odds and may rest veterans.

durable.text: He has a long record of missed games. Causes include an ongoing mystery illness plus knee and ankle problems, so experts lower his games-played projection.
He is not expected to play back-to-backs.
He is very good when he plays. His availability gets him slept on in fantasy.
He is a stretch center. He gives blocks plus threes and FT% that are well above other centers, with few turnovers. His rebounds are light for a center.

note: Our league paid 21 USD for him last season. The market now has him at 1.9 USD on Yahoo and 1.5 USD on ESPN, and the newest expert calls say not to draft him because nobody knows when he will play. With his O status and our 4 IL slots, he is at most a 1 USD end-of-draft stash for a team that wants blocks, threes and FT% from a center. The safer play is to leave him on waivers. Early in the season, watch for a real return date, whether he takes the starting center job back from Draymond Green, and his minutes. Back-to-back rest will also cost him games in the playoff weeks.
